_comment: Toolchain pin for the layout/ verification flow (klt drc / klt extract /
klt lvs), checked -- not merely recorded -- before any layout/ runner
does anything. This is a CAPABILITY list, not a version number: `klt
--version` reports klayout-tools' own static pyproject.toml version,
which can lag well behind what commands an install actually has.
`klt_required_commands` is the drift-detectable pin instead --
every layout/ runner should look each entry up in `klt --help`'s
subcommand list before doing anything else and fail loudly, naming
the missing command and the install command to fix it, rather than
skip the check silently. Keep ONE shared implementation (conventionally
`layout/toolchain_pin.py`) that every DRC/LVS/extraction runner
imports, rather than re-deriving this check per runner -- otherwise
the runners can drift apart on what they check.
THIS FILE IS A BOOTSTRAP STARTER: gf180-cryo-char has not chosen a klt pin
yet, so klt_install / klt_last_verified_commit below are placeholders,
not a foreign repo's history. Fill them in with the exact commit you
verify `klt drc` (and `extract` / `lvs`, once those runners exist)
against when this repo's layout/ harness first comes up (the standard
opening issue #2), and re-check klayout_package_min against
klayout-tools' current pyproject.toml floor at the same time. From
that point on, keep this comment APPEND-ONLY: record each later pin
bump as a new paragraph naming the issue, what changed upstream, and
why, rather than editing or deleting an earlier one. A correction to
an earlier paragraph gets its own new paragraph too -- never an edit
to the one it corrects -- so a later reader can see why the pin is
where it is without re-deriving it from git blame.
Field reference:
klt_install            exact commit to install `klt` from -- a
`pip`/`uv tool install` VCS URL pinned with
`@<sha>` (no PyPI release yet), never a
floating branch reference.
klt_required_commands  every `klt <command>` this repo's layout/
runners invoke. A missing one should be a
tooling error (exit 1) from any runner that
needs it, not a silently-skipped check.
Starts with just `drc` -- the first thing a
fresh layout/ harness wires up -- and grows
as `extract`/`lvs` runners are added.
klt_last_verified_commit  the exact commit klt_install resolves to,
restated here so it is visible without
parsing the install URL. Update both
together and re-run every runner's --check
when bumping.
klayout_package_min    floor for the pip `klayout` package version
(klayout-tools' own pyproject.toml pins a
floor of its own; recorded here so a drift
in *this* repo's pin is visible next to
klt's).
--- #4 (2026-11-26): tape-out bring-up. First extension of this file
beyond the klt pin, and the record of why each new value is where it is.
Every field below is checked -- not merely recorded -- by
layout/toolchain_pin.py, the one implementation all layout/ runners
import (build.sh --check, precheck/run.sh --check, and
verification/test_layout_toolchain.py in CI).
klt_required_commands grows from [drc] to the commands the #4 runners
call: stats and cells (read a built die back: top cell, origin, size),
diff (our build against the upstream control GDS), artifact (store a
GDS too large for git by sha256, with a committed manifest). The pin
itself does not move: 046ba74 is v0.9.2's tag commit, the release
signoff/klt-pin.txt records. Verified 2026-11-26 with
`uvx --from klayout-tools==0.9.2 klt --help`: all five commands are
listed, and that release pins klayout>=0.30, so klayout_package_min
stands. `klt drc` is still exercised by no runner here; that is the
DRC/LVS harness's own bring-up, not this one's.
die                   the wafer.space slot this repo targets: top-cell
name, slot id, width and height in um (the
3880 x 5070 um user area plus the 26 um seal
ring on every side) and the dbu. build.sh
refuses a chip_top.gds that does not read back
to exactly this.
wafer_space.pdk       gf180mcuD at the open_pdks commit both upstream
Makefiles pin and Ciel delivers (`ciel enable`).
Deliberately NOT the fleet PDK store's revision:
the DRC decks the precheck runs ship inside the
PDK, so the result is wafer.space's only on this
one.
wafer_space.template  wafer-space/gf180mcu-project-template -- the
padring, the slot definition and the example
core (never a second padring) -- with the exact
Makefile variables of upstream's own CI job:
librelane-condensed on slot 1x1 with the 5 V
foundry libraries. They are the Makefile's
defaults, written out so an upstream default
change cannot silently move the build.
wafer_space.precheck  wafer-space/gf180mcu-precheck.
Both repos are materialised on the submitting
host by `git archive` of the pinned commit and
shipped inside the job tarball: git verifies the
commit, and the token-free Spot job fetches
neither.
nix                   the Nix installer the Spot job bootstraps,
sha256-pinned. Both upstream trees lock the same
LibreLane revision in flake.lock, so `nix
develop` of the pinned tree is the toolchain
upstream's CI and Docker image run.
Size policy for the GDS itself (decided here, #4): a full-slot GDS is
~178 MB, past git's hard limit, and this repo uses no LFS. The bytes go
to the fleet artifact store (`klt artifact put`); git keeps
layout/artifacts.json, which names each by sha256, and layout/die.json,
which names the die main currently holds.
